newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly higher against the dollar on Thursday following the decline of the U.S. currency against the yen, dealers said.
"Trading was quiet today and the shekel rose slightly against the dollar following the decline of the U.S. currency in Asia," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.

"The basket (of foreign currencies) traded at the lower edge of the trading band but towards the end of the session the business sector started buying foreign currency and the Bank of Israel did not need to intervene in the market," she said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its trading band since the start of the year.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4110 shekels, against 3.4130 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7002 against 3.6992 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9502 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9339 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9748 shekels compared with 1.9725 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4105 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
